variableReadSpelling: VARIABLE-READ SPELLING (php, 2026-10-11). The `uses` targets in this file that name a `$variable` are BINDINGS, not declaration names: the analyzer spells a variable read as `<read source>\u0000<binding>` with `metadata.localBinding`, because a local/param/superglobal is never a published symbol and the BARE name let the store bind the read to an unrelated same-named declaration in another file. The defect and its counterfactual are in validation/m14/fixtures/php/local-read-phantom.mts; the whole-population effect is in docs/analyzers/history/php-lane-notes.md. What each row PINS (which read, from where, and how many) did not move.
rationale: Second PHP review wave: bare `$var` reads (frame chain, then file functions, then superglobals) and bare `NAME` const reads (file consts only). Pins the bare-foreach-value bind fix (analyzer + oracle both missed `as $item`, found only because the fixture is independent of the mirror), owner-attributed class-level reads, and the decl/write/label/type never-read positions. Every pin probe-verified against both the analyzer and derivePhpEdges before pinning; battery + lanes confirm the pair agrees on corpora. M60 (2026-09-22) re-pinned three entries in this file, deliberately and with evidence, when a callable's declaration header began being walked by the body walker (php/header-reads): a read in a parameter default or an attribute argument is attributed to the enclosing METHOD now, not to the class. The class was never the analyzer's doctrine here — it was the extracted walk's fallback (`inFunction || owner || "global"`) at a position where the walk did not know the callable and visited the header with a SUBSET of its read rules. Reverting that walk (or attributing a header read to the class again) now fails this fixture.
